Build compatibility

See which configuration fields exist on which firmware build, by REST and by CLI, and let every write skip, flag or block what a target's exact build cannot take.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsregistry.edit operations.template_approve
📍 Whereany ADOM → Automation → API → Build compatibility; API → Build compatibility for profiles without write access (Global ADOM: inside the Global block) (URL /web/registry/build-compat/); the check itself runs inside template apply, system profile and baseline apply, the carve-out push and the object editor

What is it?#

Two firmware builds that speak the same REST API version still differ in fields, and a FortiWeb write answers HTTP 200 for a field the build does not have — and silently drops it. Build compatibility checks every write against each target appliance's exact build before it is sent, and the Build compatibility page shows the field-by-build matrix behind that check.

What does it do?#

  • Reads what the API library knows about each build, by both channels: REST (sweeps, schemas, vendor data) and the CLI (tree schema and the field names show full-configuration prints).
  • Gives every field of a payload one finding per target build:
Finding Meaning Effect
missing the build has the object but not this field skipped on that appliance only, and listed
CLI only only the CLI serves it on that build warning: the REST write cannot set it
invalid option / out of range the value is not accepted by that build blocks
object absent the build's measured CLI schema has no such object blocks
unknown nothing measured this build, object or field warning: "cannot be guaranteed", never ok
  • Suggests the new name of a missing field when an operator rename map, or an equal CLI attribute id on the target build, points at one. Suggestions are never applied to the payload.

Requirements#

  • The builds you care about are in the API library: harvested from an appliance (Schema builds, API Explorer → Harvest CLI schema) or imported from an API or knowledge pack (API library).
  • For per-device checks, the appliance's firmware has been read at least once.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open the Build compatibility page registry.edit
Proceed past a blocking finding on template, profile, baseline or carve-out apply operations.template_approve plus a written reason (audited)
The checks on each write whatever that write already needs; the check adds no permission

The sidebar entry is under Automation → API when you have write access, otherwise in the API group (an API sub-menu inside the Global block in the Global ADOM). Without registry.edit the sidebar entry is not shown and the URL answers 403.

How to use#

Read the matrix#

  1. Open Automation → API → Build compatibility in the sidebar (without write access: API → Build compatibility).
  2. Pick a Product and up to eight builds. The default is the builds your fleet runs plus every build the library knows.
  3. Choose a filter: only differences (default), only CLI-only / hidden or all fields; type an endpoint or field in search. Tick the meta switch to show REST bookkeeping keys.
  4. Read each cell:
Cell Means
both REST and the CLI serve it
CLI only only the CLI serves it
hidden only show full-configuration prints it
REST only REST serves it; the build's CLI schema does not list it
CLI (REST not measured) in the CLI schema; REST was never measured for that object on that build
meta REST bookkeeping (_id, seq, q_type, *_val …), not configuration
absent measured, not there
unknown nothing measured it

Compare two builds#

  1. Under Two-build diff, pick Diff from and to.
  2. Read Objects added, Objects removed, Changed objects, Option changes, Type changes, Range changes, Default changes, Field rename candidates, Object rename candidates, Moves (same CLI id, another object) and Channel moves.
  3. A candidate that is a real rename: record it on API field renames (API library). It then shows as mapped.

Follow one field#

Click a field to open Field history: every build it was seen on, by which channel and source, and when.

What a write shows#

In the preview of a template apply, a system profile or baseline apply, a carve-out push or an object-editor save:

  • Applies, but on 8.0.6 token-secret does not exist in …: it will be skipped on 3 appliances — stripped from those appliances' payloads only;
  • … = '…' is not valid in … (allowed: …): blocked on 2 appliances — the apply is refused unless overridden;
  • not measured on 8.0.7 — cannot be guaranteed — goes ahead, unverified.

Example#

🧪Example — A template authored on 7.6.8, applied to a mixed fleet

Three appliances run 8.0.6 and two run 7.6.8. The preview says Applies, but on 8.0.6 token-secret does not exist in waf/web-protection-profile.inline-protection: it will be skipped on 3 appliances (token-secret: renamed jwt-token-secret on 8.0.6). The two 7.6.8 boxes get the full payload, the three 8.0.6 boxes get it without token-secret, and each 8.0.6 job result lists the skipped field. Adapt the template for 8.0.6 to carry the new field.

Result#

  • Skipped fields are listed in the preview and again in each device's job result.
  • A blocked apply is refused with every blocking line named; an override is audited as template.compat.override or exception.compat.override.
  • The page itself is read-only.

Troubleshooting#

"Pick at least two builds."#

Possible causes - Fewer than two builds are selected, or the product has only one build in the library.

Solution 1. Select a second build, or harvest/import another build first.

"The API library knows no build of this product yet."#

Possible causes - No appliance of that product was harvested and no pack covering it was imported.

Solution 1. Harvest an appliance from Schema builds, or import an API pack.

Hundreds of fields read unknown#

Possible causes - They belong to empty tables (or tables under a parent with no row): REST had nothing to read on that build.

Solution 1. Expected; unknown is never absent. A knowledge pack with lab rows narrows it.

"Refused by the firmware compatibility check: …"#

Possible causes - A value is not accepted by a target's build, or the object does not exist there.

Solution 1. Fix the value or adapt the template for that build; or, as an approver, give an override reason.

Verification - The next preview shows no blocking line.

Advanced#

Advanced How the check is wired

services/build_compat.py computes one view per (product, build), cached and invalidated when the product's evidence or rename maps change. Write paths call version_compat.build_check (many objects × many appliances) or version_compat.compare_object(..., values=). Per-device skips travel to the bulk runner, which strips them from that device's payload. Console equivalents: sudo satom execute apilib compat <product> <A> <B> and sudo satom execute apilib channels <product> <build> (see CLI).

Advanced Limits

A field missing from one box's configuration dump proves nothing: show full-configuration prints only the fields that apply under the row's current settings. And REST accepts a dependent field sent while its toggle is off, with 200, and drops it — send the toggle and its dependent fields in one request.

#build compatibility#firmware build#field matrix#channel#cli only#hidden field#rest only#rename candidate#cli id#skip#block#preflight
